title: One subscriber-count read can end onboarding permanently
current: If getCurrentSubreddit() returns fewer than 1,000 subscribers (or a stale, zero or missing count), onboarding saves itself as complete/ineligible and is not retried until the next install or upgrade.
evidence: Eligibility uses a single numberOfSubscribers read; !(NaN >= 1000) is also true. The subscriber_count reason is explicitly excluded from 'uncertain', so it never defers or retries. Only lifecycle reconciliation on install or upgrade re-arms onboarding.
assumptions: That Devvit can return 0 or undefined for numberOfSubscribers.
investigate: Can Devvit return 0 or undefined for numberOfSubscribers? Check the docs and installed types.
Should a below-threshold result be confirmed by a second read or re-checked periodically instead of ending onboarding?

criticality.why: A single bad read can stop a community's onboarding goal indefinitely with no visible error.
